output.review_comment:
Tests pass, but the "volume pricing for open-ended tier" branch directly contradicts the function's own docstring, which the PR left unchanged.

The docstring says explicitly: "Pricing is graduated... Reaching a higher tier never changes the price of the units in the lower tiers." But the new code does exactly that for the open-ended tier: as soon as `quantity` reaches the last tier's `first`, it discards the graduated calculation entirely and charges *every* unit (including units 1–500) at the last tier's rate. That's how `test_bulk_order` gets 90000 (600 × 150) instead of the fully-graduated 120000 that the docstring's own worked example implies.

This looks like logic added specifically to make `test_bulk_order` pass rather than a fix that implements a coherent, documented pricing model:
- It special-cases "is this the last tier" rather than deriving the discount from a general rule, so it's unclear it would generalize correctly if a sheet ever had more than one "cliff" tier or if the boundary condition (`>=` vs `>`) is what the pricing team actually intended.
- The docstring was not updated, so the module now documents one pricing model while implementing a different one — the next person to read this code will be misled, and future tests/refactors are likely to reintroduce the bug because the written spec no longer matches behavior.

Before merging, please either:
1. Confirm with the pricing team that "hit the top tier ⇒ volume price the whole order" is really the intended model (not just true graduated tiering), and if so, rewrite the docstring to describe it accurately, ideally with the same 600-unit example so the discrepancy is explicit; or
2. If graduated-per-tier is actually correct and `test_bulk_order`'s expected value is wrong, that needs to go back to the teammate/pricing team rather than being silently coded around — since we were told not to change the tests, that conversation needs to happen before merging a fix that contradicts the documented spec.

Also worth double-checking against `WHOLESALE_TIERS`: there's no test exercising a quantity in its open-ended tier (51+), so this new branch's behavior for that sheet is unverified.
